newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt concerned by German rate worries.
newsitem.headline: German debt concerned by German rate worries.

text.p: German debt closed mostly higher on Thursday after debt prices kicked off the session in a bright mood, buoyed by stronger U.S. Treasury market prices.

The September Bund futures contract, traded on Frankfurt's DTB exchange, closed trading up 22 basis points at 103.36 while the benchmark ten-year bond was at 103.74, yielding 5.49 percent, after 103.54 one day earlier.

But the short-end of the market, rattled by fears the Bundesbank might soon step in to raise interest rates, closed slower with the five year Bobl futures contract closing down three basis points at 105.16.

Dealers explained that domestic investors appeared to have been the most rattled by suggestions the Bundesbank might feel obliged to raise interest rates in order to boost the mark and stem the inflow of imported inflation.
At the moment economists say the softer mark is helping pave the way for higher import prices which will eventually filter through to the cost of living index.

In Wednesday's edition of the Handelsblatt newspaper Bundebank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick suggested the Bundesbank faced a difficult balancing act when considering both the softer mark and the fragile economic recovery.
"Currently we are playing the situation of getting out of the short end and getting into the long end," a dealer said.
Besides benefiting from the shift out of short-dated paper into longer dated funds, the longer end was also boosted by the firmer U.S. credit market.
Looking ahead dealers said U.S. data, particularly Thursday's growth data for the second quarter, would likely be very influential for the markets.
